2026-08-26T12:31:27.6091530Z ## MCP Servers Mounted as Shell CLI Commands
2026-08-26T12:31:27.6091973Z 
2026-08-26T12:31:27.6092312Z The following servers are available as CLI commands on `PATH`:
2026-08-26T12:31:27.6093316Z 
2026-08-26T12:31:27.6093780Z - `safeoutputs` — run `safeoutputs --help` to see available tools
2026-08-26T12:31:27.6094299Z 
2026-08-26T12:31:27.6096565Z > **IMPORTANT**: For `safeoutputs` and `mcpscripts`, **always use the CLI commands** listed above instead of the equivalent MCP tools. The CLI wrappers are the preferred interface — do **not** call their MCP tools directly even though they may appear in your tool list.
2026-08-26T12:31:27.6100155Z >
2026-08-26T12:31:27.6102531Z > For `safeoutputs`, treat every successful command as a real write-intent declaration. Do **not** use `safeoutputs` for exploratory probing, auth checks, placeholder payloads, repeated "try again" variants, or manual runtime experiments. When you need a safe-output, emit the final intended call once. If you are not ready to perform the real action, use `noop` or `report_incomplete` instead.
2026-08-26T12:31:27.6106649Z >
2026-08-26T12:31:27.6107489Z > For all other servers listed here, they are **only** available as CLI commands and are **not** available as MCP tools.
2026-08-26T12:31:27.6108634Z 
2026-08-26T12:31:27.6108851Z ### How to Use
2026-08-26T12:31:27.6109104Z 
2026-08-26T12:31:27.6111221Z Each server is a standalone executable on your `PATH`. Invoke it from bash like any other shell command:
2026-08-26T12:31:27.6112015Z 
2026-08-26T12:31:27.6112199Z ```bash
2026-08-26T12:31:27.6112782Z # Call a tool — pass arguments as --name value pairs
2026-08-26T12:31:27.6113528Z <server-name> <tool-name> --param1 value1 --param2 value2
2026-08-26T12:31:27.6114650Z ```
2026-08-26T12:31:27.6114894Z 
2026-08-26T12:31:27.6115191Z **Example** — using the `playwright` CLI:
2026-08-26T12:31:27.6116712Z ```bash
2026-08-26T12:31:27.6117275Z playwright --help                                  # list all browser tools
2026-08-26T12:31:27.6118082Z playwright browser_navigate --url https://example.com
2026-08-26T12:31:27.6119024Z playwright browser_snapshot                        # capture page accessibility tree
2026-08-26T12:31:27.6119780Z ```
2026-08-26T12:31:27.6119984Z 
2026-08-26T12:31:27.6120644Z **Example** — using the `safeoutputs` CLI (safe outputs) when you are ready to emit the final real action:
2026-08-26T12:31:27.6121517Z ```bash
2026-08-26T12:31:27.6122740Z safeoutputs add_comment --issue_number 42 --body "Analysis complete"
2026-08-26T12:31:27.6123440Z ```
2026-08-26T12:31:27.6123651Z 
2026-08-26T12:31:27.6123988Z **Example** — using the `mcpscripts` CLI (mcp-scripts):
2026-08-26T12:31:27.6124814Z ```bash
2026-08-26T12:31:27.6125339Z mcpscripts --help                                  # list all script tools
2026-08-26T12:31:27.6126220Z mcpscripts mcpscripts-gh --args "pr list --repo owner/repo --limit 5"
2026-08-26T12:31:27.6127220Z ```
2026-08-26T12:31:27.6127434Z 
2026-08-26T12:31:27.6127702Z ### Passing Multiple or Complex Arguments (Preferred)
2026-08-26T12:31:27.6128125Z 
2026-08-26T12:31:27.6129542Z **Preferred approach for any tool call with multiple or complex arguments**: supply a JSON object on stdin using `.` as the sentinel. The bridge parses stdin as the argument object, preserving all native types (numbers, booleans, arrays) without shell-quoting issues.
2026-08-26T12:31:27.6131131Z 
2026-08-26T12:31:27.6131304Z ```bash
2026-08-26T12:31:27.6131750Z # Full argument payload as JSON via printf pipe
2026-08-26T12:31:27.6132597Z printf '{"issue_number":42,"body":"### Title\n\nBody paragraph one.\n\nBody paragraph two."}' \
2026-08-26T12:31:27.6133417Z   | safeoutputs add_comment .
2026-08-26T12:31:27.6133746Z 
2026-08-26T12:31:27.6134224Z # Works with any tool — just match the parameter names from <server> <tool> --help
2026-08-26T12:31:27.6137453Z printf '{"title":"Fix: something","body":"Details here","labels":["bug","priority-high"]}' \
2026-08-26T12:31:27.6140977Z   | safeoutputs create_issue .
2026-08-26T12:31:27.6141499Z ```
2026-08-26T12:31:27.6141711Z 
2026-08-26T12:31:27.6142482Z **When pipes are blocked by the bash security policy**, write the payload to a file first and use **file redirection** with the `.` sentinel instead:
2026-08-26T12:31:27.6143410Z 
2026-08-26T12:31:27.6143584Z ```bash
2026-08-26T12:31:27.6145352Z # Step 1 — write the JSON payload to a file using the Write tool or a bash heredoc
2026-08-26T12:31:27.6146623Z # Step 2 — redirect the file into the CLI command using '<'
2026-08-26T12:31:27.6148305Z safeoutputs create_pull_request . < /tmp/payload.json
2026-08-26T12:31:27.6148768Z 
2026-08-26T12:31:27.6149179Z # This is equivalent to piping but does not require a separate command before '|'
2026-08-26T12:31:27.6151437Z safeoutputs add_comment . < /tmp/comment.json
2026-08-26T12:31:27.6152031Z ```
2026-08-26T12:31:27.6152236Z 
2026-08-26T12:31:27.6152463Z > **Why prefer JSON payload mode?**
2026-08-26T12:31:27.6154727Z > - Single operation for any number of arguments — no repeated `--key value` flags
2026-08-26T12:31:27.6155770Z > - Native types (integers, booleans, arrays) are preserved exactly as specified
2026-08-26T12:31:27.6157015Z > - No shell quoting or escaping needed for newlines, quotes, or special characters
2026-08-26T12:31:27.6158057Z > - Agents can construct the payload as a structured object before emitting the command
2026-08-26T12:31:27.6159279Z > - File redirection (`< file`) works even when pipes (`|`) are restricted
2026-08-26T12:31:27.6159835Z 
2026-08-26T12:31:27.6160015Z ### Notes
2026-08-26T12:31:27.6160238Z 
2026-08-26T12:31:27.6160869Z - **Prefer JSON payload mode** (`. < file` or `printf '{...}' | server tool .`) for any call with multiple arguments or complex values
2026-08-26T12:31:27.6162285Z - All parameters can also be passed as `--name value` pairs; boolean flags can be set with `--flag` (no value) to mean `true`
2026-08-26T12:31:27.6163910Z - Use `.` as the only argument to parse stdin as a JSON object (all parameters supplied at once)
2026-08-26T12:31:27.6165286Z - Parameter names with hyphens or underscores are interchangeable (e.g. `issue-number` and `issue_number` both work)
2026-08-26T12:31:27.6168121Z - Output is printed to stdout; errors are printed to stderr with a non-zero exit code
2026-08-26T12:31:27.6172056Z - Run the CLI commands inside a `bash` tool call — they are shell executables, not MCP tools
2026-08-26T12:31:27.6173118Z - These CLI commands are read-only and cannot be modified by the agent
2026-08-26T12:31:27.6173853Z </mcp-clis>
